small_guidance:
- Add more autotune configs to `conv2d_kernel` exploring smaller `BLOCK_S` (32) with `num_warps=2` and also larger tiles like `BLOCK_S=512` with `num_warps=8`; the OC=64 accumulator [64, BLOCK_S] is large, so register pressure may favor BLOCK_S=64-128 with num_warps=8.
- In `gn_apply_lse_kernel`, the [C=64, BLOCK_S] tile is reloaded from the conv output; consider larger `BLOCK_S` (1024, 2048) with `num_warps=8/16` since reduction is across only 64 channels and most cost is the load.
- Also autotune `gn_stats_kernel` (currently hard-coded BLOCK_S=2048, num_warps=8); try BLOCK_S=1024/4096 with num_warps=4/8 to reduce idle threads given CH_PER_GROUP=4 only gives 4 rows.
large_guidance:
- The conv currently uses implicit im2col with one program per (N, spatial-tile) and a full [OC=64, BLOCK_S] accumulator. Convert to a proper tiled GEMM with `BLOCK_OC` (e.g. 32 or 64) × `BLOCK_S` (e.g. 64-128) × `BLOCK_K` (IC*KH*KW = 72) so each program holds a smaller register tile and many programs run in parallel — this should better utilize SMs on the 128×128 output (S=15876).
- Fuse the conv output store with the GN-stats reduction: have the conv kernel atomically/locally accumulate per-(N, group) sum and sum-of-squares as it produces tiles, eliminating one full read of x_conv. Alternatively, use a channels_last layout for x_conv so the GN stats and apply kernels load contiguously along C.
- Consider a single-pass GN+LSE that recomputes group stats from a persistent per-row tile, eliminating the separate stats kernel; or merge stats+apply into one kernel with two passes over x_conv but only one write. Either reduces memory traffic which is currently the bottleneck given fast_p≈1.58.
